author: The Blade
title: Letter to the editor: Balanced budget not a way to rein in Social Security - NewsBreak
text:
2 hours ago
In her letter on Saturday, Kimberly English recommends a balanced budget amendment to free government money to save the Social Security system. While well-intentioned, her idea is based on a fundamental misunderstanding of how the system works.
Social Security has three sources of funding: (1) the payroll tax that workers and employers pay; (2) interest earned by the trust fund on treasury bonds that the fund is required by law to purchase; and (3) since 1983, income tax on a portion of Social Security benefits received by higher-earning recipients. Congress allocates no money to Social Security, and is prohibited by law from doing so. Why not just repeal this law? It’s part of the act that created the Social Security system in 1935; it’s the same law that prevents Congress from taking money from Social Security for other purposes. This law is the reason why Social Security made it through World War II intact. The finances of the Social Security system are independent of the federal budget. Saving money by cutting federal spending on other things cannot improve the finances of Social Security.
Social Security is running out of money for many reasons, but two are primary. First, when the system was revised in 1983, we underestimated the coming decline in the birth rate. In consequence there are fewer workers than we anticipated supporting the retirees of the baby boom cohort. Second, we underestimated the growth of income inequality; the percentage of income earned by people whose incomes exceed the tax cap has increased dramatically in the past several decades.
There are only two ways to ensure that Social Security can continue to pay full benefits after about 2033: decrease those benefits by, for example, increasing the age of eligibility for full benefits; or increase Social Security income by raising the tax or the cap on income that’s taxed. Balancing the federal budget by cutting spending — a complete impossibility in any event — would do nothing to address the problem.
GARY R. LEE
Bowling Green

RFK, Jr.’s research tampering amusing
The political cartoon on Friday showed our golf-playing President dreaming about winning the Nobel Peace Prize. You can look up the criteria for this prize and find that “Over time, the scope has expanded to include efforts in human rights …”
Right under the cartoon is a St. Louis Post Dispatch guest editorial, “RFK is turning anti-vax quackery into federal policy.”
Do you think it is a human and moral right to expect that any government, including ours, provide the opportunity for its citizens to enjoy life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness without the specter of disease and pandemics that could have been prevented through the proper administration of public health measures and research?
I find it unsettling, nay almost amusing, that one of the President’s minions is actively working to smother research into mRNA vaccines and other discoveries that will enhance our human right to life.
ERNEST LIPPERT
Toledo
A recycling program refreshing to see
The Aug. 20 edition of The Blade mentioned the recent Clean Toledo recycling program that announced the acceptance of items that in the past were refused. Items such as air conditioners, computer monitors, refrigerators, freezers, large appliances, household hazardous waste, paint, and tires. Often times, these items were refused when brought to a recycle site and, as a result, became unwanted trash strewn throughout the city.
It’s refreshing to see some people realize that the sensitive trash must be collected and disposed of properly or it will be found dumped in vacant areas less known to most residents. Hopefully, this action will be the norm in the future. Responsible citizens should take advantage of this program and do the right thing with the disposal of unique items that are no longer useful and require special treatment when discarded.
LARRY GILLEN
Maumee
Legal system limited in helping mentally ill
In his column, “Michigan’s mental health failure behind crime,” Aug. 7, Jack Lessenberry commented on a recent stabbing attack at a Walmart in Traverse City, Mich., on July 26.
Authorities found that the knife-wielding attacker, Bradford James Gille, 42, has a history of severe mental illness, including unearthing coffins to disinter a corpse. No one argues against the merits of a not guilty verdict by reason insanity in a case such as that.
Madmen with guns and knives need to be stopped, with medical intervention if possible, or dead in their tracks if need be. But suggesting the legal system can adapt some mental health cure-all for mentally challenged citizens is only wishful thinking.
Unfortunately, humanity fails to acknowledge the actual state of our eternal destiny. Our species is spiritually fallen. Even the globe herself seems to be in rebellion against us. Wildfires devour forests, wind and rain storms deluge vast areas of the planet, and wars continue to ravage innocents.
The heart of our problem is spiritual. If we think the core of societal safety revolves around medicating a crazed individual wielding a knife, we’re missing the bigger picture.
DON GOZDOWSKI
Toledo
Chamberlain’s policy followed in Ukraine
I was struck by the irony of the recent addition of the word “delulu” to the Cambridge Dictionary.
The word means “believing things are not real or true, usually because you chose to.”
As the Great Deal Maker chases the Holy Grail of a Nobel prize, it seems as if he has mistaken the peace prize for the Ignoble Appeasement Prize. History records the efforts of Neville Chamberlain to concede a portion of Czechoslovakia to Germany to avoid a future conflict. To silence public dissent, Chamberlain attempted to impose censorship. Neither strategy ended well. Now it has been proposed to reward President Putin with land acquired by military invasion and lives lost in order to avoid more of the same. Does this all sound familiar?
FRED ANDRES
Rossford
Lucas Co. officials cave to Hamas’ policy
Hamas officially controls Lucas County commissioner Pete Gerken! The FBI Joint Terrorism Task Force must investigate Gerken and the pro-Hamas agitators who bullied THE Lucas County advisory committee into “divesting” in Israel. During their screeches, none made any mention whatsoever of the hostages who are still being starved while Hamas commanders rake in billions in aid from Islamic countries. Toledo is not a playground for Hamas terrorists.
WILLIAM KENNEDY
Bowling Green
